Subject: Severe latency and 502s impacting checkout (Mar 2)

Hi Marissa,

We experienced a significant disruption today during our morning peak (approx 09:40–10:20 PST). Customers reported slow checkout flows and we saw an uptick in 502 gateway errors from calls to the embed/rerank endpoints. Latency jumped from ~120ms p50 to multiple-second tail latency; error rate spiked to ~8% in one 10-minute window. This caused timeouts in our orchestration and some abandoned carts.

Our platform team captured a few traces and attached a small sample. Can Redwood confirm root cause and provide expected timeline for mitigation and follow-up? We need a written RCA for our SRE and procurement teams.

Attachments: trace-sample-1.json (JSON), error-screenshots.zip (references)

Thanks,

Subject: Draft technical findings for Mar 2 incident — initial triage

Team — quick summary of what we’ve seen so far (initial triage):

- Timeline: 09:37 PST — traffic surge correlating with a promotional email; 09:40–09:55 — sustained 6–9x qps on rerank endpoint for ~18–20 token contexts; 09:55–10:05 — increased queueing on some GPU hosts, p95/p99 latency escalated and upstream gateway returned 502s. Root cause appears to be a combination of: (a) an unexpected traffic pattern from Acme (bursty short-context reranks), (b) a batching config that allowed very large batch-formation delays during burst arrival patterns, and (c) two GPU hosts on the same AZ experiencing transient kernel-level preemption (we saw device timeout/recover events).

- Evidence: correlation of request timestamps with host-side GPU queue depth, kernel preemption logs from hosts gpu-14/gpu-15, and ongoing elevated retry attempts from upstream load balancer. I attached the request trace samples and a trimmed export of the host logs for the 09:30–10:15 window.

- Immediate mitigations taken: scaled up dedicated pool by +20% capacity to absorb burst (automated), temporarily tightened batching max-wait from 50ms->20ms for rerank route, and circuitized two problematic hosts to shift traffic away while we investigate kernel reports. These actions brought error rate down from ~8% to ~0.6% by ~10:20 PST.

Next steps for RCA doc: full timeline, root cause (multi-factor), corrective actions (short + medium + long term), and concrete follow-through owners and dates. I’ll send a draft RCA to Marissa by EOD for customer delivery.

—Vivek
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: request-trace-logs.csv (CSV), device-timeout-snippets.txt (reference)

Subject: Final RCA and Action Plan — Mar 2 incident (attached)

Cindy / Ben —

Please find attached our formal RCA for the Mar 2 incident and the corrective-action tracking sheet (rca_mar02.pdf). Below is an executive summary and the follow-through commitments. We’ll keep your SRE and procurement teams updated weekly until all actions are closed.

Executive summary:
- Impact: Temporary spike in latency and 502 errors affecting ~3% of requests across checkout-related routes between 09:37–10:20 PST; peak error rate ~8% in a 10-minute window. No customer data loss reported.
- Root cause (multi-factor): 1) Burst traffic pattern from Acme promotional campaign amplified short-context rerank requests; 2) Batch-formation behavior allowed long wait windows during burst leading to head-of-line delays for certain hosts; 3) Two GPU hosts experienced transient kernel preemption/timeouts in the same AZ, compounding latency and triggering upstream gateway retries and 502s.

Short-term corrective actions (already applied):
- Autoscale bump and traffic shift off affected hosts (completed 09:50–10:20 PST).
- Reduced max batching wait for rerank route to reduce tail latency (completed 10:00 PST).
- Added temporary per-customer QPS cap for Acme on rerank route to smooth bursts (applied 10:05 PST).

Medium-term actions (owner and ETA):
- Host stability: run kernel-level diagnostics and replace affected nodes; owner: Vivek; ETA: 2026-03-10.
- Batching algorithm update: implement adaptive batch-window that short-circuits on bursty short-context traffic; owner: Serving Runtime team; ETA: 2026-03-24.
- Traffic shaping policy: add proactive burst protection and alerting per-customer; owner: Platform; ETA: 2026-03-17.

Long-term mitigations:
- Model routing fallbacks to less expensive/shorter-context variants for rerank under burst conditions (product + runtime; Q2 roadmap).
- Expanded cross-AZ placement rules to avoid co-locating critical hosts that could share transient underlying hardware issues.

Follow-through tracking (high level):
- SUP-2145 (incident) — status: monitoring; owner: Marissa; cadence: weekly updates w/ Acme SRE.
- JIRA tasks: SUP-2150 (batching algorithm), SUP-2151 (host replacement), SUP-2152 (traffic shaping). Links in attached doc.

Attachments: rca_mar02.pdf (PDF) — contains detailed timeline, logs excerpts, and a table of owners + target dates. Also included: request-trace-logs.csv, token-latency-sample.json.

If you’d like a walk-through of the RCA with engineering, we can set up a 30-minute meeting this week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
